metadata.note: The Kansas, Oklahoma and Gulf Railway (1919-) and its predecessor the Missouri, Oklahoma and Gulf Railway (1904-1919), the 'Muskogee Road' from Joplin and Baxter Springs through Wagoner, Muskogee, Henryetta and Durant to Denison, Texas. Drawn from research/branches/kansas_oklahoma_and_gulf_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (researched 2026-11-17). Before this layer the map drew no MO&G or KO&G route. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn, which keep to years a source confirms; most spans are [OPEN] (first/last confirmed year) or [ANCHOR] (one proven year) and say so in their notes. Rule 4 split at 1919: the MO&G (pink) and the KO&G (teal) are different operating companies; the July 1919 foreclosure sale is the change of operator. The MO&G receivership (1913-18), USRA (1919), the Texas subsidiary's 1921 rename, the KO&G receivership (1924) and Muskogee Company control (1925/26) are not splits. The Texas subsidiaries take the parent's display name and colour. Track the MO&G used by trackage rights into Joplin is drawn in MO&G colour because MO&G ran those trains. Passenger service ended in late 1954 or after; the Texas and Pacific / Missouri Pacific takeover (1963/64/70, sources conflict) came after it, so no successor feature is drawn.
metadata.omitted: [8] Dewar - Walters (Deep Fork branch, 1908 [ANCHOR], 5.8 mi): NOT DRAWN despite a drawable year - no trace of the branch survives in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap and Walters cannot be located (Nominatim knows only a 'Walters Lane'/'Walters Road' near Henryetta; Coalton geocodes 2.8 mi due north of Dewar, which does not fit an 8.26 mi branch with Walters at 5.8). Drawing it would mean inventing the geometry; it needs a located terminus first. [9] Bromide Branch, [11] KO&G Wagoner - Muskogee, [12] KO&G Wagoner - Baxter Springs, [13] KO&G Baxter Springs - Joplin and [14] the KO&G-era branches: drawable NONE (no dated passenger year) - omitted. Freight-only: Arkansas Junction - Hyde Park spur, Kenwood Junction, coal spurs around Dewar/Henryetta, all post-1954 freight years, and the north line's KO&G freight years - not drawn.

not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: every drawn span except the [ANCHOR]s is open at both ends - Wagoner - Muskogee, Muskogee - Dustin (1908-1916), Dustin - Rose (1908-1911), Wagoner - Baxter Springs and Baxter Springs - Joplin (1915-1916), and KO&G Muskogee - Denison (1926-1954). [ANCHOR] 1911: Rose - Calvin, Calvin - Red River, Red River - Denison.

UNRESOLVED 1 - north half, KO&G era: no dated passenger evidence for Muskogee - Wagoner - Baxter Springs - Joplin after 1919, though through Joplin - Denison service almost certainly ran in the 1920s. Leads: Gateway to Oklahoma History newspapers (Miami News-Record, Wagoner, Salina, Henryetta Daily Free-Lance); Oklahoma Corporation Commission annual reports (digitalprairie.ok.gov, e.g. the 16th annual report for 1923, id 140295); Stagner, 'Midland Valley: Rails for Coal, Cattle & Crude' (1996).
UNRESOLVED 2 - 1917-1925 gap, whole system: MO&G evidence stops at 1916, KO&G evidence starts at 1925w/1926. An evidence gap, not a known service gap; do not close it without a source.

UNRESOLVED 3 - exact 1954 end: the court opinion (Justia/CourtListener) and the Trains caption were not read in full (403s). Read the opinion for the application and order dates and passenger counts, and find the discontinuance date (probably late 1954 or early 1955).

UNRESOLVED 4 - Joplin alignment: MO&G's 'former route until c.1916' via South Galena - Lowell - Baxter Springs vs the Frisco Baxter Junction - Ruth / MP Ruth - Joplin route. This layer draws the former route for 1915-16; which one the Dec 1915 - June 1916 trains used is unsourced.

UNRESOLVED 5 - where the 1915-16 Joplin - OKC sleeper left the MO&G for the FS&W: Fowler shows a 'Fort Scott & Western R.R. Crossing' at MP 185.0 (between North Fork and Dustin), probably near Dustin/Weleetka. If south of Dustin, Dustin - Rose gains 1915-16.

UNRESOLVED 6 - Muskogee approach: 188.1 (1951 Guide) vs 194.5 mi (Fowler) assumed to be the 1926 Midland Valley trackage (5.8 mi, Midland Valley Junction - Muskogee). The layer draws the MV approach for both eras; the MO&G's own pre-1926 line into Muskogee is not mapped and is undrawn.
UNRESOLVED 7 - the north extension's opening: Okla. Hist. Soc. '1910' vs ICC 1912-13; ICC used.
UNRESOLVED 8 - Bromide Branch: Fowler lists Galbreath and Bromide as passenger stops with no date; a resort branch, so seasonal passenger service is plausible. Needs a dated timetable.
UNRESOLVED 9 - the 1951 index-dagger legend is OCR-garbled; index entries for Wagoner, Okay, Miami, Fairland and Salina could not be read reliably.
Dewar - Walters (1908 [ANCHOR]) is drawable but undrawn: Walters needs locating, and the branch grade is not in OSM or OHM.
Okay - Bacone river crossing: the MO&G's own bridge site is not mapped; drawn as a straight line.
Miami - Baxter Springs: the unnamed abandoned grade drawn (OSM way 440214136) is assumed to be the MO&G's own line; not confirmed.
All headway_min values except the KO&G's one-round-trip-a-day and all avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

OpenHistoricalMap was queried over every stretch and holds no KO&G/MO&G ways. Waypoints from the research report's via lists, geocoded with Nominatim (county and wrong-place answers for Wagoner, Muskogee, Mina, Rose and Bear were rejected or hand-pinned).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 16.5 mi against the documented ~16.5 mi (ICC: Wagoner - Okay 8.30, Okay - Muskogee Jct 8.30, Muskogee Jct - Muskogee 1.44; Fowler 113.6 - 130.1). Wagoner - Okay (6.9 mi) follows the abandoned grade OSM names 'Kansas Oklahoma and Gulf RR (abnd)' and an unnamed abandoned way on the same line, with 0.8 mi on the UP Wagoner Subdivision (ex-MP) at Okay. APPROXIMATED: one straight leg of 6.3 mi from Okay across the Verdigris/Arkansas rivers to Bacone (the MO&G's own Muscogee Bridge Co. crossing is not in OSM; the router otherwise put the train on the Katy's Cherokee Subdivision bridge, which is another company's track, so a labelled straight line is drawn instead). Bacone - Muskogee (3.3 mi) runs on untagged terminal track into downtown Muskogee; the MO&G depot location is not pinned, so the end is approximate to about 0.5 km.

segments.note: The first piece of the system: built 1903-04 by the Muskogee Union Railway (Wagoner - Okay 8.30 mi, Okay - Muskogee 8.30 mi, ICC), sold to the MO&G 29 Oct 1904, with the Verdigris and Arkansas river bridge by the Muscogee Bridge Co. Passenger evidence: Fowler dates Loweree 1908G (1908 Official Guide) on this segment; the Joplin - Oklahoma City joint FS&W/MO&G sleeper of Dec 1915 - June 1916 (Condren via the FS&W layer) had to use this segment to reach the FS&W. [OPEN] at both ends: 1908 is the first and 1916 the last CONFIRMED year, not known start or end dates. The wider bracket is c.1904 - 1919 (the July 1919 foreclosure sale; 1917-1919 unevidenced); the years outside 1908-1916 are an evidence gap, not a known service gap. Do not extend without evidence. From 1913 it carried the Joplin - Denison through trains; MO&G motor cars ran from 1912-13. MO&G was in receivership 12 Dec 1913 - 31 Dec 1918 and under USRA from 1 Jan 1919 - neither changed whose trains ran. No KO&G-era (1919+) passenger year has been found for Wagoner - Muskogee, so no KO&G feature is drawn here; by 1951 trains 9/10 started at Muskogee. Headway is an estimate (a few through and local trains a day) and is NOT sourced; avg_speed_kmh likewise.
sources: Segment-level: ICC valuation (construction and corporate history); Fowler t.45 (Loweree 1908G); FS&W layer citing Condren (joint sleeper Dec 1915 - June 1916). First passenger train date NOT SOURCED. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 56.5 mi against the documented 53.60 mi (ICC; Fowler 130.1 - 186.9 = 56.8). Muskogee - Midland Valley Junction (6.1 mi) is drawn over the Midland Valley's Tulsa line (OSM 'Texas and Pacific' abandoned grade and the Centennial Trail, ex-Missouri Pacific): the KO&G grade from Wainwright points straight at a junction with the MV about 3.7 mi west of downtown Muskogee (35.737N 95.482W), and the report's 188.1 vs 194.5 mi Muskogee - Denison discrepancy is assumed to be the 1926 MV trackage (5.8 mi, Midland Valley Junction - Muskogee) - unverified (UNRESOLVED 6). This stretch DOUBLE-DRAWS the Midland Valley layer's own feature 'midland-valley-muskogee-tulsa' (1906-1934). APPROXIMATED: one straight leg of 11.7 mi from Midland Valley Junction to the first surviving grade NE of Wainwright (35.592N 95.589W) - unmapped in OSM and OHM. For the MO&G era this is probably a LATER ALIGNMENT than its own era: the MO&G's own line into Muskogee before the 1926 Midland Valley trackage is not mapped anywhere, so the post-1926 approach is drawn for 1908-1916 as well. Wainwright - Henryetta - Dustin (38.8 mi) follows continuous abandoned grade OSM names 'Missouri Pacific Railroad' (the KO&G's 1964+ successor) and unnamed abandoned ways, no straight legs; Wainwright town is 3.2 km from the drawn grade, every other station under 1 km.

segments.note: Muskogee - Wainwright - Council Hill - Hitchita - Hoffman - Dewar - Henryetta - Dustin, built 1904-05 (ICC 53.60 mi); coal country. Passenger evidence: Fowler dates Midland Crossing and Frisco Crossing 1908G, Seibold 1911G, Grayson and Flushe 1914G, and Alta Vista, University Heights, Gulftown and Parsley 1915w (MO&G working timetable); the Joplin - Oklahoma City joint sleeper ran to June 1916 (where it left the MO&G for the FS&W is UNRESOLVED 5 - probably near Dustin/Weleetka). [OPEN] at both ends: 1908 is the first and 1916 the last CONFIRMED year, not known start or end dates. The wider bracket is c.1905 - 1919; the years outside 1908-1916 are an evidence gap, not a known service gap. Do not extend without evidence. The MO&G owned Dewar - Henryetta, used jointly by the Okmulgee Northern from at least 1918. Headway is an estimate (a few through and local trains a day) and is NOT sourced; avg_speed_kmh likewise.
sources: Segment-level: ICC valuation (construction 1904-05, 53.60 mi); Fowler t.45 (1908G, 1911G, 1914G, 1915w stops); FS&W layer citing Condren (joint sleeper to June 1916). First passenger train date NOT SOURCED. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 90.8 mi against the documented ~97.4 mi (Fowler 113.6 - 16.2; ICC leased lines 98.324 mi incl. the Red River bridge; Kansas piece 2.524 mi). About 7% short, mostly because four stretches are chords. Traced on ways OSM names 'KO&G' / 'KO&G RailRoad' (Wagoner - Locust Grove, Salina, Pensacola - Ketchum - Fairland - Miami, about 60 mi), then 12.6 mi Miami - Quapaw - Baxter Springs on a single unnamed abandoned grade (OSM way 440214136) running beside the Frisco's Afton Subdivision - taken to be the MO&G's own line, identity not confirmed by any tag. APPROXIMATED - straight legs: 10.7 mi Locust Grove - Salina (grade not mapped; Locust Grove is 5 km off the drawn line), 4.0 mi Salina - Pensacola, and 2.3 mi across the arm of Grand Lake o' the Cherokees between Ketchum and Fairland (grade drowned by the reservoir). Total straight: 17.0 mi.

segments.note: The north extension: Wagoner - Yonkers - Locust Grove - Salina - Pensacola - Ketchum - Fairland - Miami - Quapaw - Baxter Springs, built Jan 1912 - Feb 1913 (ICC) by two lessor companies both called the Missouri, Oklahoma and Gulf Railroad (Oklahoma, leased 99 years from 21 Sep 1912; Kansas, state line - Baxter Springs 2.524 mi, leased from 1 Feb 1913). The first MO&G train reached Miami on 14 Feb 1913 (the caption does not say passenger). CONFLICT: Okla. Hist. Soc. and Wikipedia say the extension opened 1910; the ICC valuation (primary) dates construction 1912-13 and is used. Passenger evidence: Fowler dates Spavinaw 1915w and 1916w (MO&G working timetables); the Joplin - Oklahoma City joint sleeper ran Dec 1915 - June 1916. [OPEN] at both ends: 1915 is the first and 1916 the last CONFIRMED year, not known start or end dates. The wider bracket is 1913 - 1919; the years outside 1915-1916 are an evidence gap, not a known service gap. Do not extend without evidence. No KO&G-era passenger year was found for this line (the 1951 Guide index daggers Ketchum, Locust Grove, Pensacola and Yonkers as freight-only, and it was abandoned in 1962 - an abandonment year, not a passenger end), so no KO&G feature is drawn here. Headway is an estimate (a few through and local trains a day) and is NOT sourced; avg_speed_kmh likewise.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler t.45 (Spavinaw 1915w/1916w); FS&W layer citing Condren (joint sleeper Dec 1915 - June 1916); ICC valuation (construction 1912-13); Miami history (first train 14 Feb 1913). Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 13.3 mi against the documented 15.44 mi of trackage rights (ICC). UNCERTAIN ALIGNMENT (UNRESOLVED 4): Fowler gives a 'former route until c.1916' Baxter Springs - Lowell - South Galena - Ruth (later the Southwest Missouri interurban) and a later route over the Frisco (Baxter Junction - Ruth) and the Missouri Pacific (Ruth - Joplin, 1.0 mi). This feature draws the FORMER Lowell - South Galena route, on the reasoning that 'until c.1916' covers most of the Dec 1915 - June 1916 drawable span; if the switch came before Dec 1915 the 1915-16 trains used the Frisco instead and this is the wrong alignment. Baxter Springs - Lowell - South Galena - Ruth (about 10.0 mi) follows unnamed abandoned grades OSM does not attribute to any company; the last ~3 mi into Joplin run on Frisco-tagged track (Joplin Spur / ex-Missouri & North Arkansas, 2.3 mi) and untagged Joplin terminal track, standing in for the 1.0 mi of MP track Fowler names - a later and approximate alignment. No straight legs. No other layer draws Baxter Springs - Joplin (the Frisco Wichita line feature passes north of it; no Southwest Missouri interurban layer exists), so there is no double-drawing.

segments.note: MO&G trains over other carriers' track: the ICC valuation records 'trackage rights over lines of other carriers from Baxter Springs, Kans., to Joplin, Mo., about 15.44 miles'. Okla. Hist. Soc. says trackage rights over the Frisco. Fowler: Joplin - Ruth 1.0 mi over the Missouri Pacific, Ruth - Baxter Junction over the Frisco, and a 'former route until c.1916' via South Galena and Lowell. Drawn in MO&G colour because MO&G ran these trains. The Joplin - Oklahoma City joint FS&W/MO&G sleeper (Dec 1915 - June 1916) proves MO&G passenger cars ran into Joplin. [OPEN] at both ends: 1915 is the first and 1916 the last CONFIRMED year, not known start or end dates. The wider bracket is 1913 - 1919; the years outside 1915-1916 are an evidence gap, not a known service gap. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate (a few through and local trains a day) and is NOT sourced; avg_speed_kmh likewise.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) with opstrace.py: Dijkstra over all railway ways, OSM ways whose name/operator names the KO&G ("KO&G", "KO&G RailRoad", "Kansas Oklahoma and Gulf RR (abnd)", operator="Kansas, Oklahoma, and Gulf Railway", "Durant to Denison") costed 1x as the road's own track - OSM carries no old_railway_operator tag for the KO&G/MO&G in any spelling (probed KO&G, MO&G, Kansas/Missouri, Oklahoma and Gulf) - untagged rail 1.25x (this includes the long abandoned grades OSM names 'Missouri Pacific Railroad' and 'Texas and Pacific', the KO&G's post-1964 successors), trails 3x, any other named operator 12x. OpenHistoricalMap was queried over every stretch and holds no KO&G/MO&G ways. Waypoints from the research report's via lists, geocoded with Nominatim (county and wrong-place answers for Wagoner, Muskogee, Mina, Rose and Bear were rejected or hand-pinned).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 194.0 mi against 188.1 mi (Feb 1952 Official Guide, Muskogee 0 - Denison 188.1) and 194.5 mi on the original alignment (Fowler 130.1 - 324.6). Muskogee - Midland Valley Junction (6.1 mi) is drawn over the Midland Valley's Tulsa line (OSM 'Texas and Pacific' abandoned grade and the Centennial Trail, ex-Missouri Pacific): the KO&G grade from Wainwright points straight at a junction with the MV about 3.7 mi west of downtown Muskogee (35.737N 95.482W), and the report's 188.1 vs 194.5 mi Muskogee - Denison discrepancy is assumed to be the 1926 MV trackage (5.8 mi, Midland Valley Junction - Muskogee) - unverified (UNRESOLVED 6). This stretch DOUBLE-DRAWS the Midland Valley layer's own feature 'midland-valley-muskogee-tulsa' (1906-1934). APPROXIMATED: one straight leg of 11.7 mi from Midland Valley Junction to the first surviving grade NE of Wainwright (35.592N 95.589W) - unmapped in OSM and OHM. Muskogee approach: drawn via the Midland Valley trackage for the whole 1926-1954 span (the report's assumption, UNRESOLVED 6). Wainwright - Henryetta - Dustin - Calvin follows abandoned grade OSM names 'Missouri Pacific Railroad' (successor); Calvin - Durant - Red River uses ways OSM names for the KO&G and further 'Missouri Pacific Railroad' grade; Red River - Denison is 100% the grade OSM names 'Durant to Denison'. Straight legs: the 11.7 mi Midland Valley Junction - Wainwright chord, plus three short joins where separately traced stretches meet at Dustin, Calvin and the Red River bridge (0.4, 0.4 and 0.2 mi). Station waypoints are within 1 km except Wainwright (3.2 km).

segments.note: The KO&G (incorporated 31 Jul 1919, bought the MO&G at foreclosure in July 1919) main line Muskogee - Wainwright - Henryetta - Calvin - Tupelo - Wapanucka - Durant - Denison; the 9 mi Red River - Denison belonged to the KO&G Ry. Co. of Texas. Under Muskogee Company control with the Midland Valley from 1925/26 (stock control, not a change of operator). First dated KO&G-era evidence covering the whole run is 1926 (KO&G of Texas passenger revenue $4,054, TSHA; trains could reach Denison only over the whole line; Henryetta - Calvin has Fowler 1925w). Later: Crekola 1927t, Dighton 1939G, Beland 1944G, Parsley and Mina 1947G (Fowler). In the later years gas-electric motor-car trains 9/10 (cars M-8, M-23) carried mail, express and passengers, one trip each way daily except Sunday; the Sept 1951 Guide prints the KO&G table 'No. 9 / No. 10', heading 'Motor', Muskogee 0 - Denison 188.1 - checked as rail, not bus (Condren records 'the motor from Muskogee (#9)' at the Denison yard office; the index lists the southern stops without the freight dagger). The Corporation Commission refused leave to drop trains 9 and 10 'between Muskogee and the Oklahoma-Texas state line'; the Oklahoma Supreme Court reversed on 7 July 1954 (rehearing denied 14 Sept 1954); M-23 was photographed at Denison on 8 July 1954 and scrapped 'a few months later' after the run - 'the last Muskogee Group varnish' - was discontinued. [OPEN] at both ends: 1926 is the first and 1954 the last CONFIRMED year. The bracket is 1919 - c.1954/55; 1919-1925 is an evidence gap (UNRESOLVED 2), not a known service gap, and the actual discontinuance (late 1954 or later) is undated (UNRESOLVED 3). Do not extend without evidence. After passengers: freight continued; Durant - Denison abandoned 1965 (MoPac; TSHA says the Texas trackage 1964), Muskogee - Durant abandoned 1989. Headway: one round trip a day (trains 9/10), stated in TRAINWEB and the 1951 Guide; 1440 min encodes that, and earlier decades' frequency is NOT sourced. avg_speed_kmh is an estimate - NOT computed (only one time token survives the Guide OCR).
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Feb 1952 KO&G table 9/10 and index; Kansas, Oklahoma & Gulf Ry. v. State (1954) via search summaries; Trains photo caption 8 July 1954 (snippet); Condren; TRAINWEB; TSHA (1926 passenger revenue); Fowler t.45 (1925w-1947G stops). Start 1926 and end 1954 are the confirmed floor, not service dates. avg_speed_kmh is NOT sourced.
